doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Drafted in 1963 and playing in an Army band
summary: Drafted August 1963, he ended up in an Army band; discussion of enlisting versus draft.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Did you choose to go in the service?

Well I was drafted. It was pre — it was 1963. In fact, I was thinking about that today. Today is August the 8th, and it’s Benny Carter’s 95th birthday, which is — I played with Benny Carter twice and — my idol you know. But today I thought August the 8th, that’s the day I got drafted many, many years ago.

Yeah. And so I mean in those days it was like I said pre-Vietnam when the stuff really hit the fan. And so there was no thought of resisting. People got drafted and you hoped you didn’t get drafted, but I ended up in a band and it wasn’t that bad. I practiced a lot.
Most musicians that I’ve talked to have been fortunate in that they ended up in some kind of band.

Yeah. Well the thing is you have an option. If you enlist you can pick your station — or you could then, you could pick a band and a station if you qualified. And if you get drafted it’s the luck of the draw. So if you enlist it’s three years and if you get drafted it’s two years so I just said I’ll just take my chances. So I ended up in a band. And it was okay. It was still the Army.
Oh yeah. Yeah. Like I say if somebody says were you in the service, I say yeah, our side. I fought and I fought and they took me anyway.
